name: Galahadosuchus
isnote: English Wikipedia places it in Saltoposuchidae; the atlas has no Saltoposuchidae clade, so it sits in Crocodylomorpha.
sum: Galahadosuchus is a small slender-limbed saltoposuchid crocodylomorph, probably a digitigrade runner, from the Late Triassic fissure deposits of Cromhall Quarry, England.
wsnote: No body-length estimate is given in the sources consulted.
holotype: NHMUK PV R 10002, on two slabs: a partly articulated postcranial skeleton with parts of the tail and hindlimbs, a nearly complete right forelimb, osteoderms, ribs and vertebrae, and remains of a rhynchocephalian.
biology: Likely walked on all fours with an upright digitigrade stance and was adapted for running (English Wikipedia).
author: Bodenham et al. 2026

sources.text: Bodenham, E. H., Spiekman, S. N. F., Maidment, S. C. R., Upchurch, P. and Mannion, P. D. 2026. A second species of non-crocodyliform crocodylomorph from the Late Triassic fissure deposits of southwestern UK: Implications for locomotory ecological diversity in Saltoposuchidae. The Anatomical Record.

dates_note: No PBDB occurrences. Late Triassic fissure deposits (English Wikipedia, no stage given); the ICS Carnian-Rhaetian range is used.
